title: Grateful Dead Live at Farrell Hall (SUNY) on 1970-05-08
lineage: Unknown Mic (onstage) > Cassettte Master > Sony TC-WE475 > Sony R500 (Pass Through) > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude Professional v8.01 > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Raw, tin‑can audience recording that’s hard to listen to, but a stellar Dark Star → Dancin’ stretch plus standout Good Lovin' and Uncle John’s make the show worth hunting down.
ai_review.review: The tape suffers from severe muffling, overloaded bass and stage‑mic distortion – many reviewers call it unbearable.  Despite that, the performance shines: a uniquely intense Dark Star that segues into Dancin’ In The Streets, a smoking Good Lovin' jam with a memorable Phil bass lick, and one of the most beloved Uncle John’s renditions of the era.  Listeners who can look past the audio flaws will find a historic gem.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is repeatedly praised (high‑energy Dark Star, Good Lovin', Uncle John’s) while recording quality is uniformly condemned; the weighted average yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled, tin‑can mic sound; heavy bass overload and distortion; occasional sections (Dark Star, Good Lovin') become tolerable after EQ tweaks, but overall listening is difficult.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers highlight a rare Dark Star → Dancin’ transition and note that, despite the fragmented nature of the fragment, the second‑half jam flow is exceptional.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar on Dark Star is described as "beaming" and "smoking"; strong solos in Good Lovin' are repeatedly praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a short but powerful bass solo/snatch during Good Lovin', adding depth to the jam.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum‑driven jam after Good Lovin' is singled out as amazing by several reviewers.
